narratives.Overview:
Original Tester 4 defect: #1

## Summary

Installing `@deftai/directive@0.119.0` resulted in the CLI reporting engine version 0.119.2.

## Expected behavior

The CLI should report the selected Directive version, or clearly explain any intentional engine-resolution difference.

## Actual behavior

```text
Selected package: @deftai/directive@0.119.0
directive --version:
@deftai/directive (engine: @deftai/directive-core@0.119.2)
Exit code: 0
```

## Reproduction

1. Install `@deftai/directive@0.119.0`.
2. Run `directive --version`.
3. Compare the reported engine version with the selected package.

## Environment

Windows, Node 20+, Directive package `@deftai/directive@0.119.0`, reported engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.2`.

## Impact

Version-sensitive upgrade testing and troubleshooting become ambiguous.

## Testing continuation

Testing continued, but the mismatch remained a recorded defect.

## Related GitHub issue or PR

None in `deftai/directive`. The source run was performed in `ZaenKai/directive-uat`.

Open critique of Stop 1 lean 5746989081. Charter is open critique; no refutation-target. Pin-read at dispatch-sha `7011e07402257adcda6fa496fac079cd8aa54d42`.

The P1 (banner names the engine and not the selected CLI package) is real and can bind as a reporting-identity gap. The Gate stamp's causal sentence cannot bind as written. Recut the production range and the first-semver consumers of `--version` before treating display as the whole remedy.

## Findings

### 1. sharpens-framing — published pin is `^VERSION`, not `workspace:*`

Evidence: `.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml` step "Resolve workspace protocol for npm publish" rewrites `workspace:*` to `'^' + VERSION` on `packages/cli/package.json` and `packages/core/package.json`. Registry at critique time: `@deftai/directive@0.119.0` depends on `@deftai/directive-core@^0.119.0`; `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.2` exists. For `0.y.z`, `^0.119.0` is `>=0.119.0 <0.120.0`. The UAT pair (selected `0.119.0`, engine `0.119.2`) is that range.

Failure mode: an implementer "fixes" repo `workspace:*`, or treats the workspace pin as the production pin. The published CLI keeps `^` and a later `0.119.x` core still satisfies the install.

Disposition: recut the Gate stamp from "workspace publish pins core via `workspace:*`" to "publish rewrites `workspace:*` to `^VERSION`". Record the product fork on the successor lean: exact pin at publish (stops substitution) versus keep caret and name both versions (the issue Expected's "or explain"). Do not bind a workspace-protocol edit as the remedy.

### 2. sharpens-framing — live `--version` is `dispatch.versionBanner`, not only `index.banner`

Evidence: the lean pin-read names `packages/cli/src/index.ts` `banner()`. `packages/cli/src/bin.ts` routes through `routeAndDispatch` to `packages/cli/src/dispatch.ts` `versionBanner()` (a second `CLI_PACKAGE` plus `engineInfo()`). `packages/cli/src/bin.test.ts` and `dispatch.test.ts` lock that path. SPECIFICATION.md #1918 already named both `banner()` and the version dispatch.

Failure mode: edit `index.ts` only. UAT `directive --version` does not change.

Disposition: name both copy-sites, or one shared helper, as the identity surface. `helpVersionLabel()` in the same file also keys off `engineInfo().version`.

### 3. sharpens-framing — first-semver identity consumers treat `--version` as the engine

Evidence: `packages/core/src/session/active-cli.ts` `parseVersionFromOutput` takes the first `\bX.Y.Z\b` in `--version` stdout (fallback after install-tree). `tryReadPackageVersion` on `@deftai/directive` prefers the core dep string (`^0.119.0` → `0.119.0`), not the resolved core `package.json`. `packages/core/src/resolution/classify.test.ts` `defaultEngineProbe` fixtures parse `@deftai/directive (engine: @deftai/directive-core@0.78.0)` as engine `0.78.0`. `readCorePackageVersion` (`packages/core/src/engine-version.ts`) reads the adjacent core `package.json` (the resolved engine).

Failure mode: prefixing `@deftai/directive@0.119.0` onto the banner makes first-semver parsers report the CLI package as the engine while the process still runs `0.119.2`. Ritual / #3233 and the resolution probe then disagree with `engineInfo()`.

Disposition: any dual-version banner must keep the first `\bX.Y.Z\b` as the engine, or recut those parsers in the same bind. If P1 is reporting only, record that identity gates stay core-keyed (or caret-floor-keyed) and already cannot see CLI-vs-engine skew. If P1 is substitution, the remedy is the publish range in finding 1, not the banner alone.

## Identity lens

The target is version identity of the running CLI/engine. Not untrusted input, prompts, envelopes, worktrees, or concurrency. `directive --version` is the getting-started and release-e2e identity probe. `readCorePackageVersion` is in-process identity. Caret substitution changes engine identity without changing the selected CLI package. Existing identity gates key off resolved core, first-semver, or the `^` floor. Banner-only does not close that.

## Road-not-taken

Did not treat exact publish pin as the only legal bind. Steelman of the pin: UAT selected `0.119.0` and executed `0.119.2`; Expected's "or explain" is consolation if substitution is unintended. Flip: the operator confirms caret patches are the product, then display-both (with parser coupling) is enough and an exact pin is a different issue.

## Footnotes

- footnote: git `packages/cli/package.json` `version` is `0.0.0`; publish `npm version` stamps the tarball. A dest-tree read prints `0.0.0`. Read the installed CLI `package.json` the way `readCorePackageVersion` reads core.
- footnote: published CLI also depends on `@deftai/directive-content@^0.119.0`. Same range, different surface (#3437 deposit vs content). Out of the UAT probe unless scoped in.
- footnote: SPECIFICATION.md documents the current banner shape; `index.test.ts` / `dispatch.test.ts` / `bin.test.ts` lock it. Format change is spec+test, not a new mechanism.
- footnote: `docs/versioning.md` still names Python `resolve_version` / git describe as CLI source of truth. That is not the npm `--version` path. Do not reuse it for this P1.

No `blocks-the-design`. Lean 5746989081 can bind after the three sharpenings.

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — Bound-remedy fork does not cover Stop 1 P1

Evidence: Stop 1 owns the denominator: P1 is that the banner names the engine and not the selected CLI package. Live `--version` is `packages/cli/src/bin.ts` → `routeAndDispatch` → `packages/cli/src/dispatch.ts` `versionBanner()`: constant `CLI_PACKAGE` plus `engineInfo()` from `readCorePackageVersion()`. `packages/cli/src/index.ts` `banner()` is the same shape and is locked only by `index.test.ts`. `bin.test.ts` / `dispatch.test.ts` lock the live line `@deftai/directive (engine: @deftai/directive-core@<engine>)`. Registry at this audit: `@deftai/directive@0.119.0` depends on `@deftai/directive-core@^0.119.0`; core `0.119.2` exists. Bound-remedy harvest is (1) publish rewrites `workspace:*` to `^VERSION` and a workspace-protocol edit is not the remedy, (2) an unchosen product fork: exact pin at publish versus keep caret and name both versions, (3) both copy-sites or one helper, (4) a dual-version banner keeps the first `\bX.Y.Z\b` as the engine, or recuts parsers in the same bind.

Failure mode: Spec-path harvests that list. An implementer who takes the exact-pin horn stops caret substitution. The banner still prints only the engine. Stop 1 P1 as named stays true, while `relieves: P1` stays the cite. Path-1 would treat coverage as complete.

Disposition: this map cannot bind as a P1-relieving lean. Retract `relieves: P1`. Recut Bound-remedy so every legal horn names the selected CLI package (exact pin still prints the CLI version even when it matches engine), then cite `relieves: P1` on that harvest. Leftover path if the recut still wants a remainder: bind display-both (keep caret, name both versions, first semver stays the engine, both copy-sites or one helper) as the P1 close, and file exact publish pin as a different issue. ### 2. sharpens-framing — CLI version source is the installed CLI package.json

Evidence: git `packages/cli/package.json` `"version"` is `0.0.0`; publish `npm version` stamps the tarball. `readCorePackageVersion` (`packages/core/src/engine-version.ts`) reads core `package.json` adjacent to the installed module. No CLI analog exists.

Failure mode: a display-horn harvest that says only "name both versions" lets an implementer read the git workspace file (`0.0.0`) or reuse `engineInfo().version` as the CLI package.

Disposition: on the next bind lean, add to Bound-remedy: read the installed CLI `package.json` the way `readCorePackageVersion` reads core. That changes the harvested list. Do not treat dest-tree `0.0.0` as production identity.

## Identity lens

The target is version identity of the running CLI and engine. Untrusted issue text does not set the banner. Existing identity mechanisms: `engineInfo()` / `readCorePackageVersion`; `versionBanner()` / `banner()`; `helpVersionLabel()`; `parseVersionFromOutput` in `packages/core/src/session/active-cli.ts` and in `packages/core/src/resolution/classify.ts`; `tryReadPackageVersion` (caret-floor of the core dep); `defaultEngineProbe`; `#3233` `checkActiveCliAgainstTarget`; publish rewrite to `^VERSION`. A dual-version banner whose first semver is the CLI package makes `#3233` and `defaultEngineProbe` report the CLI package as the engine while the process still runs a newer core. Bound-remedy bullet 4 covers that coupling only on the display horn. Exact pin does not create that injection and also does not name the selected CLI package.

## Road-not-taken

Rejected: both horns close the UAT mismatch, so `relieves: P1` holds. Steelman: issue Expected is report the selected version or explain the skew; exact pin removes the skew, so engine-only output that matches the selected package would turn the Tester 4 reproduction green. Flip: a new Stop 1 restates P1 as "older CLI package may run a newer unnamed engine" (mismatch), not "banner omits the CLI package". Until that restamp, the denominator is the display gap, and exact pin does not cover it.

Adoption blocker.

This is about Lifecycle: installing Directive, updating it, and getting one clear next step when something looks wrong. It also covers whether the version someone thinks they installed is the version that is actually running.

What a new person hits: The package they install resolves to a different engine than the one that actually runs.

Why that ruins the product for them: They cannot tell which product they are using. Bug reports and docs will not match what is on the machine.

How likely: High on install. Version confusion shows up before they have a project.
